title: Why You Idealise Partners: The Science Behind 'Love is Blind'
hook: Your brain distorts reality when you fall in love.

narration.text: Your brain distorts reality when you fall in love.
This happens due to a powerful mix of attachment styles and cognitive biases.
We unconsciously project our ideal partner onto the person we are with.
Our brains then filter out any information that contradicts this perfect image.
This 'idealisation bias' helps us form strong, secure bonds early on.
But it can also lead to disappointment when reality eventually sets in.
Recognising this bias helps us understand ourselves and our relationships better.
Have you noticed this idealisation in your own relationships?

description: Ever wondered why people in love seem to overlook flaws? It is not just infatuation. This short explains the psychological mechanisms, including attachment styles and cognitive biases, that cause us to idealise our partners. Understanding these processes can offer new perspectives on your own relationships.
topic: Why people in love often idealise their partners, explaining the role of attachment and cognitive biases.
